editorial.headline: Rubber Infrastructure Products, Built for Public Works Use
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22193 covers the manufacturing of rubber compounds and finished rubber goods for infrastructure, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22193 is an industrial manufacturing classification for rubber products made for infrastructure use. Its scope is not general rubber trading or a loose catch-all for rubber goods; the record points to production: rubber compounds and rubber-based items used in roads, ports, bridges, rail, canals, traffic management, and related civil works. The examples are practical and physical: rubber asphalt compound, activated natural rubber powder, dock fenders, seismic bearings, bridge bearings, rubber dams, rubber road bumps, rail pads, rail guards, canal blocking, and traffic cones.

That makes this code a home for operators whose business is built around making infrastructure-grade rubber components, not merely installing them or reselling them. The activity can sit at every scale listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain founder terms, the classification is not reserved only for large factories, although the products themselves can serve heavy-duty public or industrial environments. A small producer of qualifying rubber infrastructure goods and a larger manufacturer serving transport or civil-work demand both belong within the same scope, provided the real activity is manufacturing the goods described by the record.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That means the national entry shown here is foreign-open, without a reduced foreign stake in the slim record. The source attached to that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the record adds a special minimum capital figure, extra threshold, sector licence, or operational timeline, so none should be read into it. The strongest national conclusion is simply this: for this activity, the record treats PMA participation as open up to 100%.

Bali is also not blocked in this record, but the reason matters. The province’s moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That is not a separate Bali ownership percentage, and it is not a new cap. It is a moratorium reading: because the record places the relevant large-scale risk above the blocked Low and Medium-Low band, KBLI 22193 is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The national position is foreign-open up to 100%, and the Bali record does not mark this activity as blocked by the moratorium.
